Harness that is open source is a harness. No one is going to be a “coding” or “assistant” or “orchestrator” and a hard rule, but it’s more that each harness is kind of primed towards a particular direction. Open source means the code can be refactored to make it whatever you like.

The one difference I have seen with real significance is the typical harness vs an RLM or RSI based harness, and a couple long horizon focused harnesses. Those are not the same as codex, Claude code, or the others that have been around longer. A few of the new variants are genuinely a new paradigm and likely not a great experience for many but a lovely one for more experience developers or anyone willing to take on the extra work. The workload of the self evolving and long horizon harness is front loaded though. Eventually the threshold is reached when the model becomes more capable, flexible and just better than the human dev in general. At that point even a somewhat vague idea is likely to end up being implemented as a working solution. The harness will have built up memory, skills, and ability as it goes along the way to enable it to work much more autonomously than the previous generation of harness is capable of
